items.pronunciation_notes: The ग्र cluster runs together and the length falls on the first syllable: graa-hak.

learn.title_en: ग्राहक — the other side of दुकानदार
learn.explanation_en: ग्राहक is the customer, masculine by default and Class 2 so it never changes. It completes the pair with दुकानदार, and between them you have both sides of every shop sentence. Like other people you are being polite about, a single customer often takes plural agreement: ग्राहक आ रहे हैं. The word is Sanskrit-derived and slightly formal — in casual speech you would just as often hear लोग, people, or a name.

examples.note: Plural agreement, which also covers one customer politely.

examples.english: there are no customers in the shop
examples.note: दुकान is oblique before में, and नहीं sits in front of the verb.
पुराना is marked and agrees with the masculine ग्राहक.

common_error.why_en: ग्राहक is masculine as a word, whoever it refers to. The consonant ending predicts nothing, hence the flag.

practice.question: ग्राहक
practice.explanation_en: ग्राहक is a customer, masculine, and unchanged in the plural.

game.explanation_en: ग्राहक आना — customers come. आना is intransitive, so every tense is available.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted फ़ is an f and no vowel follows it: muft, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: मुफ़्त means free in the sense of costing nothing, and it is unmarked so it never changes. The phrase you will actually hear is मुफ़्त में, with में turning it into a manner — यह मुफ़्त में मिला, I got this free. Note that Hindi keeps free-of-charge and free-as-in-liberty entirely separate: मुफ़्त is only about money, and आज़ाद is the word for the other sense. English blurs them and Hindi does not.

examples.note: The bare adjective, unchanged for any subject.
मिलना is intransitive, so the perfective works now.
की agrees with चीज़, which is feminine.

common_error.why_en: मुफ़्त takes no endings at all. Adding -ी to make it feminine produces a word that does not exist.

practice.question: मुफ़्त
practice.explanation_en: मुफ़्त is free of charge. आज़ाद is free in the sense of liberty.

game.question_en: Which postposition turns मुफ़्त into free of charge?
game.explanation_en: मुफ़्त में मिलना — में makes it a manner, like आराम से and प्यार से.

items.pronunciation_notes: Breathy ध in the middle and the length on the second syllable: u-dhaar.

learn.title_en: One noun, two verbs, two opposite meanings
learn.explanation_en: उधार is credit or borrowing, masculine and uncountable. Hindi has no separate words for borrow and lend — it has one noun and lets the verb decide. उधार लेना is to borrow, उधार देना is to lend, and the noun is identical in both. This is the same two-sided pattern as छूट मिलना against छूट देना, and it is worth noticing as a general habit of the language rather than a quirk of one word.

examples.note: लेना for borrowing, and the future is safe with a transitive verb.
देना for lending — the same noun, the other direction.
उधार पर means on credit, and मत negates the imperative.

common_error.why_en: देना means you are the one lending. If you want to borrow, the verb is लेना.

practice.question: उधार
practice.explanation_en: उधार is credit or borrowing, and the verb decides which direction it goes.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with उधार when you are the borrower?
game.explanation_en: उधार लेना is to borrow. उधार देना is to lend, with the same noun.

summary.recap_en: The shopping block is complete at fifteen words. उधार is the clearest case of a habit this module keeps showing: one noun with two verbs pointing in opposite directions — लेना to borrow, देना to lend — where English needs two separate words.
summary.next_up_en: Next: cooking, starting with the verb that covers almost all of it.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three syllables with the length on the middle one: ba-naa-naa.

learn.title_en: खाना बनाना is how Hindi says cook
learn.explanation_en: The ordinary way to say cook in Hindi is खाना बनाना — to make food. There is a verb पकाना that means cook specifically, but बनाना is what people actually say, and it covers making anything at all: चाय बनाना, खाना बनाना, घर बनाना. Note the shape of the word. बनाना is the transitive partner of बनना, to be made, formed by inserting a long aa — the same pattern that gave चलाना from चलना and लगाना from लगना.

examples.note: The habitual — बनाना is transitive, so the perfective waits for Module 9.
The तुम imperative, and the same verb covers tea.
बनना, the intransitive partner — nobody is named as the cook.

common_error.why_en: करना is the default guess for almost everything and it is wrong here. Food is made, not done.

practice.question: बनाना
practice.explanation_en: बनाना is to make, and खाना बनाना is the ordinary way to say cook.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with खाना when you cook?
game.explanation_en: खाना बनाना — food is made rather than done.

items.pronunciation_notes: Unaspirated p at the front, so no puff of air: pa-kaa-naa.

learn.explanation_en: पकाना is to cook in the narrow sense of applying heat until something is done. बनाना is to prepare a dish. So you पकाना a vegetable and बनाना a meal, and if you are talking about dinner in general बनाना is what people say. पकाना is the transitive partner of पकना, to be cooked or to ripen — which is why fruit ripening is also पकना. The insert-a-long-aa pattern is now three for three: बनना to बनाना, पकना to पकाना, चलना to चलाना.

examples.note: The तुम imperative, with a specific dish as the object.
पकना, the intransitive partner, with nobody named as the cook.
The same verb for fruit ripening, since both are things reaching doneness.

common_error.why_en: Not wrong, but it sounds oddly technical. For cooking a meal in general, people say बनाना.

practice.question: पकाना
practice.explanation_en: पकाना is to cook something through. बनाना is the general word for preparing a meal.

game.question_en: Which verb is the intransitive partner of पकाना?
game.explanation_en: पकना — the food cooks by itself. Remove the long aa and you get the intransitive.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three vowels in a row at the end with no consonant between: ra-so-ii.

learn.explanation_en: रसोई is the kitchen, and it ends in -ई, which as level twenty-three showed is as reliable a feminine marker as -ी. So this one you can predict without being told. It declines like नदी: रसोई में in the singular, रसोइयों में in the plural. The English किचन is also widely used and neither is more correct. रसोई also has an older sense of cooked food itself, which survives in the word रसोइया, a cook.

examples.note: रसोई is oblique before में, though nothing visible changes.
साफ़ is unmarked and never changes.
छोटी is feminine, which confirms रसोई is.

common_error.why_en: Words ending in -ई are reliably feminine, so a marked adjective takes -ी.

practice.question: रसोई
practice.explanation_en: रसोई is the kitchen, and its -ई ending makes the feminine gender predictable.

game.question_en: Which postposition goes with रसोई for being inside it?
game.explanation_en: रसोई में — में for being inside a room.

summary.recap_en: खाना बनाना is how Hindi says cook, and पकाना is the narrower verb for cooking something through. Both follow the insert-a-long-aa pattern that turns an intransitive verb into its transitive partner — बनना to बनाना, पकना to पकाना.
summary.next_up_en: Next: spice, oil and the dishes — the three things a Hindi kitchen runs on.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three syllables with the length on the second: ma-saa-laa.

learn.title_en: मसाला is a mixture, not a single spice
learn.explanation_en: मसाला is masculine and Class 1, so its plural is मसाले and its oblique plural मसालों. The word usually means a blend rather than one ingredient — गरम मसाला is a mixture, and मसाला डालो means add the spices. English borrowed it back as masala. Its verb is डालना, to put in or pour, which is what you use for adding anything to a pot. डालना is transitive, so use it in the imperative or the present for now.

examples.note: The तुम imperative — डालना is transitive.
The plural मसाले with a plural verb.
मसालों is the oblique plural before की, which agrees with the feminine ख़ुशबू.

common_error.why_en: मसाला ends in -ा, so it is Class 1 and must go oblique before a postposition.

practice.question: मसाला
practice.explanation_en: मसाला is spice, usually a mixture rather than one ingredient.

game.explanation_en: मसाला डालना — डालना is what you use for adding anything to a pot.

items.pronunciation_notes: One syllable with a clear e and a dental त: tel.

learn.title_en: तेल covers cooking oil and hair oil alike
learn.explanation_en: तेल is masculine, flagged, and uncountable so it has no plural. It covers any oil at all — cooking oil, engine oil, and the hair oil that is a daily fixture in most Indian households, so तेल लगाना means to oil your hair rather than to grease a pan. Its cooking verb is डालना, the same as मसाला. Note that तेल is dental — the tongue touches the teeth — which separates it from the retroflex sounds in English loanwords.

examples.note: The same verb as with मसाला.
गरम is unmarked and never changes.
ख़त्म होना means to be finished, and it is intransitive.

common_error.why_en: तेल is uncountable and has no plural, so the verb stays singular.

practice.question: तेल
practice.explanation_en: तेल is oil of any kind, masculine, and it has no plural.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with तेल in cooking?
game.explanation_en: तेल डालना for adding it to a pan. तेल लगाना means applying it to hair or skin.

items.pronunciation_notes: The र is a light tap against the त that follows: bar-tan.
items.gloss_en: a dish, a pot, a utensil

learn.title_en: बर्तन covers every vessel in the kitchen
learn.explanation_en: बर्तन is any kitchen vessel — a pot, a pan, a plate, a bowl. There is no separate everyday word for washing-up, so बर्तन धोना is the whole chore. It is masculine, flagged, and Class 2, so the plural looks identical to the singular and only the verb tells you which you mean: बर्तन गंदा है for one, बर्तन गंदे हैं for the pile. धोना is transitive, so keep it out of the perfective for now.

examples.note: The तुम imperative of धोना.
The plural shows only on गंदे and हैं, since बर्तन is Class 2.

examples.english: there are dishes in the kitchen
examples.note: रसोई is oblique before में.

common_error.why_en: बर्तन is masculine and Class 2, so the plural is identical to the singular. -ें is a feminine plural ending.

practice.question: बर्तन
practice.explanation_en: बर्तन is any kitchen vessel — pot, pan, plate or bowl.

game.explanation_en: बर्तन धोना — and that phrase covers the whole washing-up.

summary.recap_en: डालना is the kitchen's general-purpose verb for adding anything to a pot, and it covers both मसाला and तेल. बर्तन is Class 2, so its plural is invisible and only the adjective and verb tell you how many there are.
summary.next_up_en: Next: cutting, boiling, and the word for fresh.

items.pronunciation_notes: Retroflex ट with the tongue curled back, and no vowel before the न: kaaṭ-naa.

learn.explanation_en: काटना is to cut, and it stretches a long way: cutting vegetables, cutting hair, a mosquito biting, and — usefully — spending time, as in दिन काटना, to get through a day. In the kitchen it is what you do before anything else, so सब्ज़ी काटो is the first instruction in most recipes. It is transitive, so its perfective काटा needs ने and is not yet available; the imperative and the continuous are.

examples.note: The तुम imperative — काटना is transitive.
The continuous, which is safe with any verb.
The same verb, since a bite is a kind of cut.

common_error.why_en: करना is the reflex guess again. Vegetables are cut, and करना would say nothing at all about what you are doing to them.

practice.question: काटना
practice.explanation_en: काटना is to cut, and it also covers biting and getting through time.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with सब्ज़ी before you cook it?
game.explanation_en: सब्ज़ी काटना — chopping comes before cooking.

items.pronunciation_notes: Four syllables with the length on the second: u-baal-naa.

learn.title_en: उबालना and उबलना — who is doing the boiling
learn.explanation_en: उबालना is to boil something, and उबलना is for something to boil by itself. That is the insert-a-long-aa pattern for the fourth time: चलना to चलाना, लगना to लगाना, बनना to बनाना, and now उबलना to उबालना. The rule is worth trusting now — if you meet a new verb and need the version where someone is doing it to something, try lengthening the vowel. मैं पानी उबालता हूँ, I boil water; पानी उबल रहा है, the water is boiling.

examples.note: The transitive form — you are doing it to the water.
The intransitive उबलना — nobody is named.
The perfective is available because उबलना is intransitive.

common_error.why_en: The long aa makes it transitive, which would mean the water is boiling something else. Water boils by itself.

practice.question: उबालना
practice.explanation_en: उबालना is to boil something. उबलना is for something to boil by itself.

game.question_en: Which form do you use when the water boils by itself?
game.explanation_en: उबलना, without the long aa. Adding it makes someone else responsible.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ज़ buzzes between two long aa vowels: taa-zaa.

learn.title_en: ताज़ा agrees, and it covers news as well as food
learn.explanation_en: ताज़ा is fresh and it is marked, so it agrees: ताज़ा, ताज़ी, ताज़े. Like महँगा and सस्ता it is one of the few adjectives in this module that changes at all. It applies to food, air and news alike — ताज़ी ख़बर is the latest news — exactly as fresh does in English. Its opposite for food is बासी, stale, which despite ending in -ी is unmarked and never changes.

examples.note: खाना is masculine, so the adjective takes -ा.
सब्ज़ी is feminine, so the adjective takes -ी.
बासी ends in -ी and is unmarked, like दुखी and ज़रूरी.

common_error.why_en: सब्ज़ी is feminine, and ताज़ा is a marked adjective, so it has to follow.

practice.question: ताज़ा
practice.explanation_en: ताज़ा is fresh, and it agrees with the noun it describes.

game.explanation_en: सब्ज़ी is feminine, so the marked adjective takes -ी.

summary.recap_en: The long-aa pattern has now appeared four times — चलना/चलाना, लगना/लगाना, बनना/बनाना, उबलना/उबालना — and it is reliable enough to use on verbs nobody has taught you. ताज़ा agrees; its opposite बासी looks feminine and does not.
summary.next_up_en: Next: taste and spiciness, and a conversation over the stove.

items.pronunciation_notes: The स्व cluster is a single sound with no vowel between: svaad.

learn.title_en: स्वाद आना — the flavour comes to you
learn.explanation_en: स्वाद is taste or flavour, masculine and flagged. Its verb is आना, so खाने में स्वाद आया means the food tasted good — literally flavour came into the food. There is also the adjective स्वादिष्ट, delicious, which is unmarked and slightly formal; in everyday speech people are more likely to say खाना अच्छा है or बहुत स्वाद है. This is the same आना you met with ग़ुस्सा, हँसी and नींद.

examples.note: खाना goes oblique to खाने before में, since it is Class 1.
अच्छा is masculine, agreeing with स्वाद.
स्वादिष्ट is the adjective, unmarked and a little formal.

common_error.why_en: स्वाद is masculine. The consonant ending gives no clue, which is why it is flagged.

practice.question: स्वाद
practice.explanation_en: स्वाद is taste or flavour, and it is masculine.

game.explanation_en: स्वाद आना — the flavour comes, like ग़ुस्सा and हँसी before it.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ज़ is a z, so the word ends in a buzz: tez.
items.gloss_en: spicy; also fast, sharp, bright, strong

learn.title_en: One word for spicy, fast, sharp and bright
learn.explanation_en: तेज़ is unmarked and covers a remarkable range: spicy food, a fast car, a sharp knife, a bright light, a strong fever, a clever student. The common thread is intensity, and context does all the work. In the kitchen it means spicy, and खाना तेज़ है is what you say when your mouth is burning. Note that it is not the same as गरम, which is hot in temperature — food can be गरम without being तेज़ and the reverse.

examples.note: In the kitchen तेज़ means spicy rather than hot.
The same word doing an entirely different job.
Intensity again — the thread running through all its senses.

common_error.why_en: गरम is hot in temperature. If your mouth is burning from chilli, the word is तेज़.

practice.prompt_en: What does this word mean when talking about food?
practice.question: तेज़
practice.explanation_en: तेज़ is spicy. गरम is hot in temperature, and the two are different things.

game.question_en: Which adjective describes food that burns your mouth?
game.explanation_en: तेज़ for chilli heat. गरम is temperature only.

items.pronunciation_notes: The three verb words run together at speed: ba-naa ra-haa huuṁ.

learn.title_en: The continuous is right here, and the habitual would not be
learn.explanation_en: तुम क्या बना रहे हो asks what you are making at this moment, so the continuous is correct — the habitual would be asking what you cook in general, which is a question about your repertoire rather than your evening. The last line hangs on gender: स्वाद is masculine, so अच्छा rather than अच्छी. Note also that खाना appears twice in this module with two jobs, as the noun for food and as the verb to eat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: हाँ, थोड़ा तेज़ है, लेकिन स्वाद अच्छा है।
lines.read_as: haaṁ, thoṛaa tez hai, lekin svaad achchhaa hai.
lines.english: Yes, a little spicy, but it tastes good.

common_error.why_en: स्वाद is masculine, so the adjective takes -ा. The consonant ending is no help at all.

practice.question: मैं खाना बना रहा हूँ
practice.explanation_en: The continuous present — cooking is happening right now.

game.question_en: Listen to the last line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: स्वाद is masculine, so the adjective is अच्छा.

tts_strings: हाँ, थोड़ा तेज़ है, लेकिन स्वाद अच्छा है।

summary.recap_en: The cooking block is complete at twelve words. स्वाद takes आना like every other sensation in this module, and तेज़ means spicy rather than hot — गरम is temperature, and confusing the two is the difference between a warm plate and a burning mouth.
summary.next_up_en: Next: relationships and society, then the city and its services.
